name: token-pace
description: Quota, tokens and API cost for Claude Code and Codex, permanently in the status bar — coloured by pace, not by level.

commands.title: Token Pace: Reset Network Access Decision

enumDescriptions: Extra/purchased usage on top of the plan
Total tokens used today across both tools

tokenPace.statusBar.show.markdownDescription:
Which entries the status bar shows. Use `#tokenPace.windows#` to control how many quota windows each tool contributes.

An empty list hides the status bar entirely.

enumDescriptions: Quota bars with the elapsed-time tick
Token totals for today / 7 days / 30 days
Stacked chart of the last 14 days

tokenPace.dashboard.sections.markdownDescription: Which sections the **Token Pace** panel shows, in fixed order.

enumDescriptions: Every quota window as its own entry — including model-scoped ones (e.g. “7 d · Fable”)
Only the most-utilised window per tool
tokenPace.windows.markdownDescription: Which quota windows appear in the status bar.

tokenPace.barWidth.markdownDescription: Bar width in characters. `0` hides the bars.

enumDescriptions: Thin baseline (▁) as the track — quiet, recommended
Dotted shading (░) — more contrast, grainy at small font sizes
No track, only the filled part
tokenPace.barStyle.markdownDescription: How the **empty** part of the bar is drawn.

tokenPace.showCost.markdownDescription:
Show the **API cost** column: what this usage would have cost through the provider API at list prices.

This is a hypothetical figure. On a subscription you do **not** pay these amounts — there is no billing relationship.

tokenPace.alignment.markdownDescription: Right-aligned entries are hidden **without notice** when the window is narrow. `left` is recommended.

tokenPace.staleAfterMinutes.description: Age from which a quota figure counts as stale and is greyed out.

enumDescriptions: Read the cache file; offer once to fetch if nothing is there (recommended)
Fetch directly from the provider — requires your one-time consent
Only read the cache file, never fetch and never ask
tokenPace.quotaSource.markdownDescription:
Where the quota figures come from. Token counts come from local transcript files either way and never need network access.

`auto` (default) reads only the cache file that an external poller (panel plugin, cron job) may write, and **makes no network access of its own**. If nothing is there, it offers once to switch to `poll`.

`poll` fetches directly: the access token from `~/.claude/.credentials.json` goes to `api.anthropic.com`, and the local `codex app-server` is started. This happens only after you have explicitly agreed in a dialog that states exactly what is sent. The token is only read, **never refreshed**, and never logged.

`cache` settles the question for good: cache file only, no offer.

tokenPace.pollIntervalMinutes.markdownDescription: Interval between the extension's own fetches, in minutes. Only applies where fetching actually happens (see `#tokenPace.quotaSource#`). Failures trigger a growing backoff (429: up to 2 h, network: up to 30 min).

tokenPace.claudeDir.markdownDescription:
Claude Code's directory. Empty = `~/.claude` (on Windows `%USERPROFILE%\\.claude`), or `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` if that was set when VS Code started.

Takes effect after **Reload Window**.

tokenPace.codexDir.markdownDescription:
Codex's directory. Empty = `~/.codex`, or `CODEX_HOME` if that was set when VS Code started.

Takes effect after **Reload Window**.

tokenPace.claudeQuotaFile.markdownDescription:
JSON file holding the Claude quota state. Empty = `~/.cache/claude-usage/state.json`.

This file is written by an **external poller**, not by Claude Code itself.

tokenPace.codexQuotaFile.markdownDescription: JSON file holding the Codex quota state. Empty = `~/.cache/codex-usage/state.json`. See the note on `#tokenPace.claudeQuotaFile#`.

tokenPace.codexBinary.markdownDescription: Path to the `codex` executable. Empty = `CODEX_CLI_PATH`, then `PATH`, then the binary bundled with the official IDE extension.
